Subject: FinPay: follow-up & TCO comparison vs hyperscalers

Hi Olivia / Tom 

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap from today's discovery
- Primary goal: move inference off the managed hyperscaler endpoints to reduce unit costs while keeping p95 latency <= 200ms for interactive flows.
- Workload: conversational customer support, avg response length ~120 tokens, peak concurrency ~60 RPS (spiky), expected monthly usage ~50-150M tokens.
- Non-negotiables: SOC2 / audit logs, region data residency, and predictable SLA for peak windows.

What we proposed
1) Competitive TCO comparison (Redwood vs OpenAI / AWS Bedrock) with scenarios for batching and KV prefix caching.
2) Short technical test: 24-48h perf run using your top 20 prompts (we'll A/B Redwood vs your current endpoint).
3) Security/compliance next steps - I'll loop our security lead for the questionnaire.

Immediate next steps
- I've attached an initial TCO model (redwood_tco_model.xlsx) with assumptions and line items. Please give me the cost and latency numbers you currently see (samples or aggregate) so we can populate the model.
- If OK, Marcus and I can spin up the A/B test next week - suggested window Tue/Wed.

Can you confirm:
- Procurement point of contact (Tom?)
- A set of priority prompts we should use for the A/B?

Thanks - happy to sync for 30m if that helps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Aditya - good recap. A few clarifying items before we run the A/B: 

1) Can you give a quick ballpark on per-1M token unit economics for the three scenarios you mentioned on the call:
   - baseline (no batching / no caching)
   - batching enabled (what batch size / latency tradeoff assumed)
   - caching / cache hit assumptions (how much does prefix/KV caching reduce token compute)

2) How do you compare vs the hyperscalers on p95 latency under similar load? Our current target is p95 <= 200ms and we'd like to understand how realistic 100-150ms is.

3) Procurement question: for Dedicated/reserved capacity pricing, what minimum commitment are we looking at? Tom's looped in - he needs rough order numbers to prep the finance team.

We'll pull together the 20 prompts and send them by EOD. Also attaching one sample trace from our current endpoint (we'll send the file separately).

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinPay: follow-up & TCO comparison vs hyperscalers

Great questions - below is a concise breakdown with the assumptions used in the attached model. The spreadsheet has the line-by-line math; below are the headline numbers so you can share with procurement.

Assumptions (short)
- Model family: 30B gen model (comparable quality to current gen you're using)
- Avg response: 120 tokens generated per call
- Token ratio (input+output): 1.3x
- Baseline batch size = 1; batching scenario batch size = 16 (effective throughput gains shown)
- KV/prefix cache hit: low = 20%, med = 50% (we show both)

Headline unit economics (per 1M generated tokens) - Generation-only component (USD):
- Baseline (no batching, no cache):
  - Redwood hosted: $3.50 per 1M tokens
  - OpenAI (comparable): $5.00 per 1M tokens
  - AWS Bedrock: $6.20 per 1M tokens

- With batching (target batch size 16, typical utilization on your workload):
  - Redwood effective: $0.65 per 1M tokens
  - OpenAI effective (if using their batching): $1.20 per 1M tokens

- With batching + caching (50% cache hit on generation prefix / KV reuse):
  - Redwood effective: $0.35 per 1M tokens
  - OpenAI effective: $0.80 per 1M tokens

Notes on the math: the model separates compute, mem/KV, infra overhead, and network. Redwood benefits more from batching and long-lived KV cache because our runtime merges requests and amortizes kernel setup and cross-GPU communication. The spreadsheet shows per-token compute seconds, assumed GPU cost curve, and batching efficiency factors.

Latency guidance (p95)
- Baseline single-request p95 (no batching): Redwood hosted typical p95: 120-180ms (model and prompt dependent).
- With batching: p95 can increase depending on batch latency target; we typically bound batching to keep added queuing < 30-50ms. Example: target batch size 16 + max queue delay 50ms -> observed p95 ~ 160-220ms on similar workloads.
- On dedicated capacity with tuned batching and prefix cache, customers often see p95 in the 90-140ms range for short-to-medium prompts. We'll validate with your prompts in the A/B.

Procurement / Dedicated commit
- Reserved/Dedicated minimum typically starts at a 3-month commit for pilot-sized pools (~1-2x of your peak), pricing is provided as a monthly committed amount plus lower per-token unit costs. I'll have our pricing team provide a committed quote once we have an expected monthly token target from you.

Next steps I recommend (short):
1) Share the 20 prompts and a week of representative traffic patterns (timestamps + volumes).
2) Marcus and I run a 24-48h A/B: Redwood vs your current endpoint (we'll instrument p95, p50, errors, and cost per call).
3) We'll populate the TCO model with your actual counters and share a side-by-side.

Attach: latency_report.pdf (pdf, 85KB) - includes sample p95 curves from a recent similar customer. Also see redwood_tco_model.xlsx for the detailed assumptions.

If that looks good, Marcus and I can book the test Wed/Thu next week. Tom - we can share a pilot committed pricing range once Olivia confirms expected monthly tokens.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Hi Olivia / team - quick tech plan from my side so the A/B is high-signal and actionable: 

Proposed test plan (24-48h)
1) Test workload: your 20 prompts, mixed with synthetic variation to match peak ratios (we'll ask for a 7-day sample to build the pattern).
2) Load profile: run 3 windows - low, median, peak (peak = 60RPS sustained bursts).
3) Batching config: target_batch_size = 16, max_queue_ms = 50. We'll also run a control with batch_size = 1 to measure baseline p95.
4) KV/prefix cache: enable prefix caching for the top 10 prompts; measure cache hit rate and synthetic 20/50/80% hit simulations.
5) Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/day, compute seconds, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens (from model).
6) Failure modes: we'll inject a 10% error burst to validate graceful fallback (route to spare capacity or smaller model).

Deliverables
- A/B report (p50/p95, error rates, cost delta)
- Populated TCO model with your real counters
- Short checklist for Dedicated sizing if you want reserved capacity post-pilot

Scheduling
- Marcus: available Tue/Thu next week for the test window (or we can do Wed/Thu per Aditya suggestion). Propose 30m sync on Mon to confirm prompts and traffic file.

Let me know a good time for the short prep call. I can also share an automated script that pumps the exact request shapes so you can replay locally if preferred.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
